stETHFundamental.$comment: stETH PRIMARY, pure fundamental: stETH/ETH is held at 1.0 (Lido's redemption invariant), matching how wstETH (stEthPerToken x ETH/USD) and eETH (1.0 x ETH/USD) are priced. Replaces the market stETH/ETH CrossRate primary, which is demoted to a monitor as stETHCrossRate. Deployed from eETH_CustomPriceFeed - a unit-rate BaseCustomPriceFeed - so the contract name on the explorer reads eETH while the priced asset is stETH: ugly by name, clean by bytecode, and it reuses already-reviewed code. Requires _deployEEth to be parameterised by config key (see _deployNxm / _deployOsToken for the existing precedent). PARAMETERISE ALL THREE ROLES, not just the constructor-arg reads: (1) the _readAdapterDeployed("priceFeeds", name) idempotency probe, (2) the readPriceFeedParam(..., name, ...) reads, and (3) the writeAdapterAddress(..., "priceFeeds", name, ...) write. _deployEEth currently hardcodes "eETH" in all three. Parameterising only (2) would write this feed's address into deployments.customPriceFeeds under the key 'eETH', silently repointing eETH's own feed at a stETH-bound contract, and (1) would then skip the deploy entirely once 'eETH' exists. The CustomFeedAssetMismatch guard would catch that crossing at RegisterAssets time rather than letting it ship, but it still costs a deploy round-trip.

ETHxCrossRate.$comment: ETHx redundancy feed (ETHx_CrossRateCustomPriceFeed). CrossRate: ETHx/USD = ETH/USD x ETHx/ETH, with ETH/USD read from the NAV (ADR 0019). yToXFeed MIGRATED 2026-07-27 from the Redstone Classic Push ETHx/ETH feed (0xc799194cAa24E2874Efa89b4Bf5c92a530B047FF) to Chainlink because Redstone is sunsetting all its ETHx feeds. CORRECTED 2026-07-30: that migration pointed at 0xC499ec76e2F5ac15e127A352Bc40cF24FC472401, which is the raw ACCESS-CONTROLLED AGGREGATOR, not its EACAggregatorProxy. It passes every inspection a config review would run - description() == "ETHx / ETH", decimals 18, and latestRoundData() answers a cast call - yet NO CONTRACT can read it: Chainlink's SimpleReadAccessController grants access only when _user == tx.origin, so a direct EOA eth_call succeeds while every contract is denied (measured: checkEnabled() == true, hasAccess(<contract>,"") == false, hasAccess(<EOA>,"") == true). OracleArgumentChecks.assertChainlinkOracle probes latestRoundData() in a try, is denied, and the constructor reverts NotChainlinkOracle() - so _deployEthxCrossRate() (03_DeployPriceFeeds.s.sol:211 -> :639; ETHx uses that NAMED deploy function, not the generic _deployCrossRateMonitor) reverted during 03_DeployPriceFeeds simulation, and because vm.writeJson side effects are NOT rolled back on revert that run left phantom customPriceFeeds addresses in deployments/1.json which 04 then collided with. yToXFeed is now the PROXY 0xC5f8c4aB091Be1A899214c0C3636ca33DcA0C547, sourced from Chainlink's reference-data-directory (name "ETHx / ETH", proxyAddress 0xC5f8c4aB..., contractAddress 0xC499ec76..., decimals 18) and independently corroborated on-chain by the aggregator's AddedAccess(0xc5f8c4ab...) event at block 20270750. Proven with four checks: aggregator() == 0xC499ec76... (proves the proxy sits above exactly the aggregator that was configured, not a same-named different feed), description() == "ETHx / ETH", decimals() == 18, and CONSTRUCTIBLE FROM A CONTRACT on a fork (the property that was actually missing - a passing cast call proves nothing here, which is how the bad address passed review). Note description() was CORRECT on the bad address, so a description-based pair assertion would NOT have caught this. There is NO Chainlink ETHx/USD feed (FeedRegistry.getFeed reverts "Feed not found"), so the ETH-quoted cross-rate is the only Chainlink route. The 18 decimals need no config change: TwoFeedChainlinkPriceFeed captures 10**rateFeed.decimals() in its constructor, so the rate decimals cancel into NAV_DECIMALS. Independent of the primary ETHx feed (Stader on-chain rate) in both source and methodology; serves as ETHx's monitor feed.

ezETHCrossRateMarket.$comment: ezETH MARKET divergence monitor — the SECOND monitor for ezETH, added alongside (never replacing) ezETHCrossRate. Closes audit finding #2: ezETH's primary is Renzo's RestakeManager rate (fundamental) and its only existing monitor, ezETHCrossRate, was migrated 2026-07-22 to RedStone's ezETH_FUNDAMENTAL feed, so the divergence check compared one fundamental rate against another. The source was independent; the methodology was not. Two fundamental sources agreeing says nothing about market price, so ezETH's 250 bps tolerance could not fire on the depeg it exists to catch. Post-ADR-0019 both legs read base/USD from the same NAV, so the ETH/USD term cancels exactly and the comparison reduces to rate-vs-rate with no residual signal. yToXFeed here is the RedStone Classic Push ezETH/ETH MARKET feed 0xF4a3e183F59D2599ee3DF213ff78b1B3b1923696 — the feed ezETHCrossRate used before the migration. NOTE it is recorded as SUNSET by RedStone (Slack C03BP6L2A9W / Nicolas) and IS DEPRECATED, which is deliberate and safe here for three reasons: (1) it is a MONITOR, never a primary, so it can never price the NAV; (2) monitors are heartbeat-gated in PriceFeedLib._readFeedPrice, which returns (0,false) past the heartbeat, and _monitorDivergence does `if (!ok) continue` — so a frozen feed SELF-EXCLUDES rather than contributing a stale rate, and monitorFeedCount drops 2->1 making the degradation observable; (3) the downside is therefore bounded to today's behaviour while the upside is real depeg detection immediately. MEASURED, not assumed, over 64 AnswerUpdated events across 29.5 days (rounds 1988-2051): the feed is very much alive - gaps median 43212 s, MAX 43224 s, jitter 12 s, unimodal at 12 h (57 of 63 intervals; the other 6 are all SHORTER, i.e. deviation-triggered, which means during a real depeg it publishes EARLY and is freshest exactly when it matters). yToXHeartbeat 46800 = max observed gap 43224 + 3576 s margin (8.3%, ~298x the observed jitter). NOT 86400 (that was copied from the fundamental feed's config and would treat ~12 h of frozen data as fresh) and NOT 43200, which would sit 24 s TIGHTER than the observed max - the exact finding-#8 trap of setting a heartbeat equal to the publisher's cadence. The reason for the tight heartbeat is to halve the detection latency of the monitor's OWN DEATH, NOT to prevent false alarms: measured primary drift is +0.595 bps/day (ezETH fundamental rate moved +16.30 bps over 27.38 days, ~2.17%/yr restaking yield), so a frozen monitor would need ~389 days to false-trip 250 bps. Divergence tolerance stays 250 bps, confirmed against a distribution rather than one sample: market-vs-fundamental spread over 331 samples / ~27.5 days was min 7.85, median 18.39, p90 27.90, max 37.55 bps, never above 50 - 6.7x headroom - with market BELOW fundamental in 331/331 samples (a persistent 8-38 bps discount with a stable sign, which is what a depeg detector wants: it fires on the magnitude growing off a steady baseline). Deployed via the GENERIC _deployCrossRateMonitor("ezETHCrossRateMarket") since this constructor block matches that helper's shape; the raw feed CANNOT be registered as a monitor directly because monitors are compared in USD while this feed reports ezETH/ETH (~1.08e8), so against the primary's ~2063e8 it would read ~9994 bps and mark ezETH permanently irregular. The CrossRateCustomPriceFeed wrapper returns NAV_DECIMALS (8), satisfying MonitorFeedDecimalsMismatch.

wARS.$comment: wARS ('Peso Argentino'). The ARS Chainlink feed KPK uses is quoted USD / ARS (0xBb65fa58BDb7d33e4a3D1A40a7A9BD99E746367b, description() == 'USD / ARS', 8 decimals, ~158309760000 = 1583.09 ARS per USD, verified on-chain 2026-08-15). That is the RECIPROCAL of the asset/USD direction every primary feed here uses, so it CANNOT be registered as type 'Chainlink': doing so would price 1 wARS at ~$1,583 instead of ~$0.00063, an over-report of ~2.5 MILLION x. InvertedChainlinkCustomPriceFeed inverts it (1e8 * 10^feedDec / answer, division last). The param is named *ChainlinkAddress so RateFeedGuard._isRateFeedParam recognises it and the guard below is MANDATORY rather than silently skipped. baseAsset is 0x0 and that is an ASSERTION, not an omission: this feed reads no base/USD out of the NAV, and PriceFeedLib._validateFeedNotCircular probes BASE_ASSET() by raw staticcall and FAILS CLOSED (CustomFeedBaseUnreadable) on a feed that cannot answer - so the contract implements INavSourcedPriceFeed and returns address(0), as ETHPlus_CustomPriceFeed does. The deploy helper does not pass this key to the constructor; it exists so the feed stays inside preflight's circularity checks. HEARTBEAT: MEASURED on-chain 2026-08-15 over 13.2 days of AnswerUpdated on the aggregator 0xc30fB86c2559E4B757C037976e3244901c10FAf8: 30 updates, min gap 84s (deviation-triggered), median 23928s, MAX 86436s (24.01h), 8 gaps EXCEED 86400 and 0 exceed 90000. So 86400 would have gone stale 8 times in 13 days; 90000 has zero breaches with ~1h headroom. The pair is absent from chainlink_declared_heartbeats.json, so preflight can only WARN 'no declared heartbeat recorded' - this measurement is the evidence in its place, not a guess at a declared value.

rateFeedGuard.$comment: Pins BOTH the pair and the DIRECTION. description() == 'USD / ARS' catches a swap to any other pair; the band catches an inverted feed even if a description were forged - an ARS/USD feed would answer ~0.00063 (6.3e14 at 1e18 scale), FIVE orders below the floor (1e10 / 67207 ~= 1.5e5). Band is deliberately wide upward because ARS is a high-inflation currency and this rate only rises: 1583 today, ceiling 100000 allows ~63x further depreciation; floor 100 allows ~15x appreciation. THE FLOOR'S REAL TRIGGER IS REDENOMINATION, NOT APPRECIATION - read it that way before acting on it. ARS appreciating 15x is essentially impossible, so framed as an appreciation bound the floor looks like it guards nothing; the event it actually catches is a currency redenomination, which arrives as a single announced step rather than gradually. Argentina has dropped 13 zeros across five of them (1970, 1983, 1985, 1992, and the 2025 'peso sin ceros' three-zero bill). A 1,000:1 redenomination takes the published rate 1583.0976 -> 1.5831, about 63x BELOW the floor, and the floor firing there is CORRECT: an ERC20 wrapper cannot redenominate without a token migration, so a feed with no floor would keep valuing each un-redenominated wARS at ~1,000x its true worth. THE CORRECT RESPONSE IS A TOKEN/FEED MIGRATION REVIEW - NEVER widen the floor downward. Widening it is precisely the action that reinstates the 1,000x over-report, and a stale-looking feed after a redenomination is the moment someone is most likely to reach for it. Verified live on-chain 2026-08-15.

wARS.$noNavDependencyReason: This feed reads NO base/USD price out of the NAV. It derives wARS/USD wholly from one Chainlink leg by inverting it (1e8 * 10^feedDec / answer), so there is no base asset to read and BASE_ASSET is a compile-time constant address(0) on the contract, not a configurable argument. The zero here MIRRORS the contract rather than opting out of a dependency that exists. REQUIRED whenever baseAsset is 0x0: the sentinel switches off both the base-allowlist and the derived-heartbeat checks, so pasting it onto a genuinely NAV-sourced feed would otherwise pass preflight silently and fail only when 03 reverts mid-run with earlier feeds already broadcast.
wARS.$directFeedComment: NOT the only ARS feed on mainnet - a DIRECT ARS/USD feed exists at 0xE41cD2DcC63EB63A9D9e62f2a3D9b49e6d0C0A1d (8 dec, answer 67207 = $0.00067207, verified on-chain 2026-08-15) and would need no custom contract. The two disagree by ~6.4% ($0.00063167 inverted vs $0.00067207 direct), persistently. USD/ARS is used DELIBERATELY because it is the reference the vault accounts in, and it is the conservative of the two. OPEN: the direct feed is a free independent monitorFeed and is not wired - wARS currently has one primary, zero monitorFeeds and no pegToleranceBps, so PriceFeedLib._hasDivergenceChecks is false and `irregular` can never fire. The baseline 640bps gap exceeds every divergenceToleranceBps in this repo (50 and 250), so wiring it needs a tolerance with no local precedent - a decision for the operator, not a default.
wARS.$bandComment: MIN/MAX_ANSWER are the RUNTIME direction pin, in the feed's own 8 decimals: 100e8 .. 100000e8 vs a live 1583.0976e8. RateFeedGuard pins the same band but is DEPLOY-ONLY, so it cannot see a Chainlink proxy that later migrates its aggregator at the same address with the same decimals. An ARS/USD re-quote would answer ~0.00067e8 = 67207 raw, FIVE orders BELOW the floor (1e10 / 67207 ~= 1.5e5), so the band catches the re-quote that decimals() cannot. Keep these in step with rateFeedGuard.minRate1e18/maxRate1e18.

WBTCCrossRate.$comment: WBTC divergence MONITOR (ChainlinkCrossRateCustomPriceFeed), issue #356. WBTC/USD = Chainlink 'WBTC / BTC' (0xfdFD9C85aD200c506Cf9e21F1FD8dd01932FBB23, 8 dec, ~0.99816 at block 26240000) x Chainlink 'BTC / USD' (0xF4030086522a5bEEa4988F8cA5B36dbC97BeE88c, 8 dec), both read DIRECTLY from Chainlink. WHY A MONITOR: WBTC's primary is Chainlink BTC / USD, which prices BITCOIN, not the token, so a WBTC depeg is invisible to it; mainnet has no Chainlink WBTC / USD, so the WBTC-specific price has to be composed. WHY NOT CrossRateCustomPriceFeed: that class reads its base/USD leg back out of the NAV, and the NAV prices BTC/USD on WBTC itself, so registration would reject it (IPrices.CustomFeedBaseCircular, PriceFeedLib._validateFeedNotCircular - enforced on addMonitorFeed too). baseAsset is 0x0 and that is an ASSERTION, not an omission: the contract's BASE_ASSET is a compile-time constant address(0); 03 asserts it pre-broadcast (_assertNoNavDependencyFeedsDeclareZeroBase) and does not pass this key to the constructor. HEARTBEATS EQUAL THE CHAINLINK DECLARED VALUES (ADR 0025), checked against reference-data-directory feeds-mainnet.json 2026-10-22: WBTC / BTC heartbeat 86400 (0.5% deviation), BTC / USD heartbeat 3600 (0.5% deviation). Staleness per ADR 0029: a leg past its heartbeat keeps the price and flags it stale; updatedAt is the older leg's timestamp. description() of both feeds verified live on-chain 2026-10-22.

rateFeedGuard.$comment: Pair identity + plausibility band for the WBTC / BTC rate leg (rateChainlink). description() verified live on-chain 2026-10-22. Band 0.5 .. 1.5 BTC per WBTC, deliberately WIDER than a parity wrapper needs: this feed exists to SEE a depeg, and a rate outside the band makes the feed report (0, stale) - i.e. the monitor goes unhealthy instead of raising `irregular`. A 0.5 floor keeps every depeg short of a 50% collapse inside the band, where it surfaces as `irregular` against the BTC / USD primary. The band still catches a re-pointed aggregator: BTC / USD answers ~8e12 raw and ETH / BTC ~3e6, both orders of magnitude outside. The BTC / USD leg (baseUsdChainlink) has no guard block - RateFeedGuard pins one param per instance - and is asserted by description() in the fork test instead.

WBTCCrossRate.$noNavDependencyReason: This feed reads NO base/USD price out of the NAV. It derives WBTC/USD wholly from two Chainlink legs (WBTC / BTC x BTC / USD), so there is no base asset to read and BASE_ASSET is a compile-time constant address(0) on the contract, not a configurable argument. The zero here MIRRORS the contract rather than opting out of a dependency that exists - and a NAV-sourced base is not possible for this asset at all, because the NAV's BTC/USD base is WBTC itself.
WBTCCrossRate.$bandComment: minAnswer/maxAnswer are the RUNTIME pin on the rate leg, in WBTC / BTC's own 8 decimals: 0.5e8 .. 1.5e8 vs a live ~0.998e8. RateFeedGuard pins the same band pre-deploy and reconciles these two keys against rateFeedGuard.minRate1e18/maxRate1e18 (RateFeedBandMismatch), so they cannot drift.

WBTCCrossRateRedstone.$comment: Second WBTC depeg MONITOR (issue #356): the same ChainlinkCrossRateCustomPriceFeed class as WBTCCrossRate, with RedStone's WBTC/BTC push feed 0xD260596f85C6D91Ccd40f7076eEb62ACb3B2ad53 as the rate leg (description() 'RedStone Price Feed for WBTC/BTC', 8 decimals, verified on-chain 2026-10-22; RedStone default trigger 0.5% / 86400 s) and Chainlink BTC/USD as the base. Source redundancy for the WBTC-specific price, and with two monitors WBTC is not reported monitorsUnhealthy during the ~30 s a day the Chainlink WBTC/BTC round overshoots its heartbeat. Over 88 days |RedStone WBTC/BTC - 1| peaked at ~32 bps, below the 50 bps tolerance. The constructor param is named rateChainlink only because the deploy helper is shared; the feed is any AggregatorV3-compatible rate feed. HEARTBEAT 86400 (ADR 0025): RedStone's default push trigger for this dataFeedId is 0.5% deviation or 86400 s (ethereumMultiFeed manifest, no per-feed override); measured over 88 days to 2026-10-22: never deviation-triggered; sampled hourly, 72 of 110 push intervals were at or past 86400 s (typically 86412-86436 s, max 89688 s), so this monitor drops out for a block up to ~55 min on most days. That overlap with the Chainlink WBTC/BTC leg's own ~30 s overshoot is rare, so the pair still keeps WBTC out of monitorsUnhealthyPriceAssets almost always. 86400 stays (ADR 0025: registered == declared). Checked by redstone_declared_heartbeats.py, which reads custom-feed RedStone legs since issue #356; the fork test pins the leg's identity.
WBTCCrossRateRedstone.$noNavDependencyReason: Same as WBTCCrossRate: both legs are read directly from AggregatorV3 feeds (RedStone WBTC/BTC x Chainlink BTC/USD) and multiplied in the feed; nothing is read back out of the NAV, so BASE_ASSET() returns address(0). A NAV-sourced base is impossible here: WBTC IS the NAV's BTC/USD asset, and registration rejects a feed whose base is the asset itself (CustomFeedBaseCircular).

rateFeedGuard.$comment: Pair identity + plausibility band for the RedStone WBTC/BTC rate leg; description() verified live on-chain 2026-10-22. Same 0.5 .. 1.5 band and reasoning as WBTCCrossRate.

syrupUSDG.$comment:
syrupUSDG primary (syrupUSDG_CustomPriceFeed, a thin ERC4626VaultRatePriceFeed subclass - sibling of syrupUSDC, same Maple `MaplePool` code over a different underlying). Price = (USDG/USD) x convertToAssets(1 share), the USDG/USD leg read from the NAV (ADR 0019).

THIS FEED COULD NOT HAVE EXISTED BEFORE 2026-09-16: its base asset is USDG, which was registered that day. The base's BaseAssetMismatch check enforces the pairing (baseAsset_ must equal the vault's asset()), so a copy-paste of the syrupUSDC block would revert at construction rather than price USDG shares against USDC.

MANIPULATION GATE (docs/howto/add-price-feed.md): MaplePool.totalAssets() forwards to IPoolManagerLike(manager).totalAssets() - cash plus loan principal plus accrued interest - NOT balanceOf(vault). Measured live 2026-09-16: totalAssets 168,376,875.642470 USDG against a vault USDG balance of 8,060,166.467433, so cash is ~4.8% of assets and the share rate is not donation-spikeable the way a naive balance-of vault is.

KNOWN LATENT PROPERTY, shared with the LIVE syrupUSDC feed: MaplePool.convertToAssets divides the RAW totalAssets() by supply while the pool's own convertToExitAssets first subtracts unrealizedLosses(). The base prices with convertToAssets, so on a loan default this over-reports until Maple realises the loss. Both Maple vaults read unrealizedLosses() == 0 on 2026-09-16, so the two paths agree exactly today; this is recorded so it is not rediscovered as a surprise.

Registered to make the Aave V4 UsdgMapleE Spoke (0x774b9655413c34809c1f1b16b654465A89EBE989) usable: syrupUSDG is its r1 COLLATERAL-ONLY reserve, with USDG (r0/r3) and USDC (r2) borrowable and already registered.

LBTC.$comment:
LBTC PRIMARY (LBTC_CustomPriceFeed, a BaseCustomPriceFeed subclass). LBTC/USD = LBTC.getRate() (BTC per LBTC, 18-dec) x WBTC/USD read from the NAV (ADR 0019).

THE RATE IS READ ON-CHAIN BECAUSE LBTC IS YIELD-BEARING. Babylon staking rewards are converted to BTC and reflected in a rising LBTC->BTC exchange rate rather than in holders' balances (the implementation behind the LBTC proxy is named StakedLBTC), so LBTC is the same shape as rETH, wstETH and ezETH - each of which is priced on THIS chain from its own on-chain rate, with market feeds used only as monitors. (cbETH follows the same pattern where it is deployed, but is not a chain-1 asset, so it is not cited here as a local peer.) An earlier revision of this config had the Chainlink LBTC/BTC MARKET feed as the primary; that was wrong for this asset class and is now the monitor (LBTCCrossRateMarket below).

BASE = WBTC, and that is not a WBTC bet: the NAV prices WBTC with the Chainlink BTC/USD feed (0xF4030086522a5bEEa4988F8cA5B36dbC97BeE88c), so WBTC/USD IS BTC/USD and the product is exactly (BTC per LBTC) x (BTC/USD). WBTC is priced by DIRECT feeds rather than another NAV-sourced custom feed, which is what NavBaseUsdLib's circularity invariant requires of a base.

THE RATE IS STEPWISE AND CAN FALL - do not treat it as a floor. Sampled every 3 days over 60 days: flat at 1.004899545 from 30d to 21d, then -1.80, -0.83 and -4.57 bps to a trough of 1.004179667 at 12d, recovering to 1.005005450. Three decreases in 20 intervals, ~7.2 bps peak-to-trough, against a long-run trend of ~+16.6 bps over 180 days. Lombard's docs call the update 'continuous'; the chain does not agree.

LBTCCrossRateMarket.$comment:
LBTC MARKET divergence monitor (generic CrossRateCustomPriceFeed), NOT the primary. LBTC/USD = WBTC/USD x Chainlink LBTC/BTC.

ITS JOB IS METHODOLOGY INDEPENDENCE, not just source independence - the same role ezETHCrossRateMarket plays for ezETH. The primary reads Lombard's own on-chain rate, which does not observe market price at all, so a market discount on LBTC cannot move it. It CAN still fall for protocol reasons - measured, 3 decreases in 20 intervals over 60 days - so the claim is specifically that it cannot fall BECAUSE the wrapper is trading below par, not that it cannot fall. This leg is a market price (the feed's reference-data attributeType is `dex_state_price`, assetSubClass `Pegged Asset`), so it can. Both legs read WBTC/USD from the same NAV, so the base term cancels exactly and the divergence check reduces to rate-vs-rate with no residual signal.

It CANNOT be registered as a raw monitor feed: monitors are compared in USD and the underlying Chainlink feed reports an LBTC/BTC ratio (~1.0e8), so against a ~76,000e8 USD primary it would read ~9,999 bps and mark LBTC permanently irregular. The CrossRate wrapper returns NAV_DECIMALS (8), satisfying MonitorFeedDecimalsMismatch.

TOLERANCE SET ON MEASUREMENT: market-vs-fundamental spread sampled every 2 days over 90 days, 46 samples - |spread| min 0.01, median 5.07, p90 13.18, MAX 19.63 bps, with market BELOW fundamental in 35 of 46 (the persistent small discount a liquid wrapper carries). divergenceToleranceBps 100 is therefore ~5.1x the observed maximum: tight enough to fire well before a real depeg, loose enough that the steady baseline never trips it. Deliberately far tighter than the 250 bps the ETH LSTs carry, because this spread is an order of magnitude smaller than theirs.
LBTCCrossRateMarket.$heartbeatComment: yToXHeartbeat 86400 = EXACTLY the declared value (ADR 0025). Measured over 40 rounds / 39 intervals: min 86,400 / median 86,424 / max 86,448 - 39 of 39 at or past declared, so the Chainlink LBTC/BTC feed is purely HEARTBEAT-driven. On a MONITOR that zero margin does not zero an asset: a monitor past its heartbeat self-excludes in PriceFeedLib._readFeedPrice and monitorFeedCount simply drops, which is observable rather than silent.

rateFeedGuard.$comment: Pair identity + plausibility band for the rate feed named by `param`, enforced pre-deploy by RateFeedGuard (fail-closed: a rate-feed param with no guard block reverts RateFeedGuardMissing). description() read live on-chain 2026-09-16; the feed is the PROXY (aggregator() returns 0x3F6047b77131ce78Ab4775feE2d38b7339471a01, so registering the aggregator would freeze silently at Chainlink's next rotation).
rateFeedGuard.$bandComment: LBTC is 1:1 BTC-backed, so the honest band is tight around parity - live value 1.00453494. [0.90, 1.10] catches CROSS-CLASS confusion outright (a BTC/USD feed here would read ~76,000) and a grossly broken or renamed feed, while leaving room for the premium/discount a market rate can carry under stress. It is a DEPLOY-TIME plausibility check, not a runtime guard: nothing re-checks the band after deployment.

syrupUSDT.$comment:
syrupUSDT primary (syrupUSDT_CustomPriceFeed, a thin ERC4626VaultRatePriceFeed subclass). Price = (USDT/USD) x convertToAssets(1 share), the USDT/USD leg read from the NAV (ADR 0019). Third member of the Maple family on this chain after syrupUSDC and syrupUSDG - same MaplePool code, different underlying - so the pricing logic is deliberately identical across all three.

REQUESTED for the XAUt carry fund's syrupUSDT leg: before this feed isAssetRegistered(syrupUSDT) was false and getPriceData reverted, so a syrupUSDT position did not appear in NAV at all.

BASE = USDT, which was already registered and priced by a DIRECT Chainlink feed (0x3E7d1eAB13ad0104d2750B8863b489D65364e32D) - what NavBaseUsdLib's circularity invariant requires of a base, and it means the share is valued with the same USDT/USD price every other USDT leg uses. The base's BaseAssetMismatch check enforces the pairing against the vault's own asset(), so a copy-paste of the syrupUSDC or syrupUSDG block reverts at construction rather than pricing against the wrong dollar. Both sides are 6-dp, so there is no decimals offset.

MANIPULATION GATE (docs/howto/add-price-feed.md) CHECKED: MaplePool.totalAssets() forwards to IPoolManagerLike(manager).totalAssets() - cash plus loan principal plus accrued interest - NOT balanceOf(vault). Measured live 2026-09-17: totalAssets 336,758,291.074368 USDT against a vault USDT balance of 642,712.210795, so cash is 0.19% of assets - a WIDER margin than syrupUSDG's 4.8%. Live rate at registration: 1.143506 USDT per share.

SAME LATENT PROPERTY as its siblings: MaplePool.convertToAssets divides RAW totalAssets() by supply while convertToExitAssets first subtracts unrealizedLosses(), so on a loan default this over-reports until Maple realises the loss. unrealizedLosses() reads 0 on all three Maple vaults on 2026-09-17.

LIQUIDITY IS NOT PRICE: syrupUSDT redemption is not instantaneous - kpk's own Maple risk assessment (risc PR 106, overall score 4; zero on-chain collateral on the USDT loan channel, first-loss cover 0, top-3 borrower concentration 66.8%) records a withdrawal pending far beyond the ~5-minute median. This feed reports a MARK, not an exit price; do not read it as redeemable-on-demand value when sizing redemptions.
